3. How many sequences are BFRB vs. non-BFRB (`sequence_type`)? Is there class imbalance at the gesture level?

```{python}
#| echo: false
# sequence-level BFRB vs non-BFRB counts (one row per sequence)
seq_level = (
    train_df
    .group_by("sequence_id")
    .agg(
        pl.col("sequence_type").first(),
        pl.col("gesture").first(),
        pl.col("is_bfrb").first(),
    )
)

seq_type_counts = seq_level["sequence_type"].value_counts().sort("sequence_type")

bfrb_seq_counts = seq_level["is_bfrb"].value_counts().sort("is_bfrb")

    seq_level

axes[1].invert_yaxis()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Sequence Anatomy

5. What are the typical lengths (in rows) of the Transition, Pause, and Gesture phases within a sequence?

```{python}
#| echo: false
# what phases actually exist?
print(train_df["phase"].unique().sort())

# per-sequence length for each phase
phase_lengths = (
    train_df
    .group_by("sequence_id", "phase")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("length"))
)

# summary stats per phase
summary = (
    phase_lengths
    .group_by("phase")
    .agg(
        pl.col("length").mean().alias("mean"),
        pl.col("length").median().alias("median"),
        pl.col("length").std().alias("std"),
        pl.col("length").min().alias("min"),
        pl.col("length").max().alias("max"),
        pl.len().alias("n_sequences"),
    )
    .sort("phase")
)
print(summary)

# distribution plot
phases_present = train_df["phase"].unique().sort().to_list()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(phases_present), 1, figsize=(8, 4 * len(phases_present)))
if len(phases_present) == 1:
    axes = [axes]
fig.suptitle("Phase Length Distribution (rows per sequence)")

for ax, phase in zip(axes, phases_present):
    lengths = phase_lengths.filter(pl.col("phase") == phase)["length"].to_numpy()
    ax.hist(lengths, bins=40)
    ax.set_title(phase)
    ax.set_xlabel("rows")
    ax.set_ylabel("# sequences")
    ax.axvline(lengths.mean(), color="red", linestyle="--", label=f"mean={lengths.mean():.0f}")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

6. Is phase length consistent across subjects and gestures, or highly variable?

```{python}
#| echo: false
# join gesture and subject onto phase lengths
phase_lengths_detail = (
    train_df
    .group_by("sequence_id", "phase")
    .agg(
        pl.len().alias("length"),
        pl.col("gesture").first(),
        pl.col("subject").first(),
    )
)

# variability by gesture: focus on Gesture phase
gesture_phase_var = (
    phase_lengths_detail
    .filter(pl.col("phase") == "Gesture")
    .group_by("gesture")
    .agg(
        pl.col("length").mean().alias("mean_len"),
        pl.col("length").std().alias("std_len"),
        pl.col("length").median().alias("median_len"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("std_len") / pl.col("mean_len")).alias("cv")  # coefficient of variation
    )
    .sort("mean_len", descending=True)
)
print(gesture_phase_var)

# visualize gesture-phase length spread
gestures = gesture_phase_var["gesture"].to_list()
means = gesture_phase_var["mean_len"].to_numpy()
stds = gesture_phase_var["std_len"].to_numpy()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 8))
y = np.arange(len(gestures))
ax.barh(y, means, xerr=stds, align="center", alpha=0.7, capsize=4)
ax.set_yticks(y)
ax.set_yticklabels(gestures, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Gesture-phase length (rows) ± 1 std")
ax.set_title("Gesture Phase Length by Gesture: Mean +/- Std")
ax.invert_yaxis()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# does gesture-level CV survive controlling for subject, or is it just between-subject noise?
subj_gesture_var = (
    phase_lengths_detail
    .filter(pl.col("phase") == "Gesture")
    .group_by("subject", "gesture")
    .agg(
        pl.col("length").mean().alias("mean_len"),
        pl.col("length").std().alias("std_len"),
        pl.len().alias("n"),
    )
    .filter((pl.col("n") >= 3) & (pl.col("mean_len") > 0))
    .with_columns((pl.col("std_len") / pl.col("mean_len")).alias("within_subject_cv"))
)

within_subject_cv_by_gesture = (
    subj_gesture_var
    .group_by("gesture")
    .agg(pl.col("within_subject_cv").mean().alias("avg_within_subject_cv"))
)

# compare ranking: uncontrolled (mixed-subject) CV vs. within-subject CV
compare_cv = gesture_phase_var.select(["gesture", "cv"]).join(
    within_subject_cv_by_gesture, on="gesture", how="inner"
).sort("cv", descending=True)
print("Uncontrolled CV vs. within-subject CV by gesture:")
print(compare_cv)

rank_corr = compare_cv.select(
    pl.corr("cv", "avg_within_subject_cv", method="spearman").alias("rank_corr")
).item()
print(f"\nSpearman rank correlation (uncontrolled vs within-subject CV): {rank_corr:.2f}")
```

## Sensor Modality Availability

8. Which sequences have full sensor data (IMU + thermopile + ToF), and which are IMU-only?

```{python}
#| echo: false
core_cols = (
    ["acc_x", "acc_y", "acc_z", "rot_w", "rot_x", "rot_y", "rot_z"]
    + [f"thm_{i}" for i in range(1, 6)]
)

# null counts per core column
null_counts = train_df.select(pl.col(core_cols).is_null().sum())
print("Null counts per core sensor column:")
print(null_counts)

# rot and thm_5 are the problem sensors: confirm they are independent failures
overlap = train_df.with_columns([
    pl.col("rot_w").is_null().alias("rot_missing"),
    pl.col("thm_5").is_null().alias("thm5_missing"),
]).group_by("rot_missing", "thm5_missing").agg(pl.len())
print("\nRot vs thm_5 missingness overlap (zero overlap = independent failures):")
print(overlap)

# how many sequences are fully missing thm_5?
total_seqs = train_df["sequence_id"].n_unique()
thm5_dead_seqs = (
    train_df.group_by("sequence_id")
    .agg(pl.col("thm_5").is_null().mean().alias("pct"))
    .filter(pl.col("pct") == 1.0)
)
print(f"\nSequences with thm_5 fully dead: {len(thm5_dead_seqs)} / {total_seqs} ({len(thm5_dead_seqs)/total_seqs:.1%})")

# flag thm_5 absence, fill with mean; forward-fill rot within sequence
train_df = train_df.with_columns([
    pl.col("thm_5").is_not_null().cast(pl.Int8).alias("thm5_present"),
    pl.col("thm_5").fill_null(pl.col("thm_5").mean()),
])
rot_cols = ["rot_w", "rot_x", "rot_y", "rot_z"]
train_df = train_df.with_columns(
    pl.col(rot_cols).forward_fill().over("sequence_id")
)
```

10. Does `-1` in ToF columns mean no object detected, or does it indicate sensor failure? How frequent is it and does its frequency vary by gesture?

- a -1.0 represents there is no sensor response, as per the official documentation

```{python}
#| echo: false
tof_cols = [f"tof_{s}_v{v}" for s in range(1, 6) for v in range(64)]

# overall -1.0 rate
overall_rate = train_df.select(
    pl.mean_horizontal([(pl.col(c) == -1.0).cast(pl.Float32) for c in tof_cols]).mean().alias("overall_tof_missing_rate")
).item()
print(f"Overall ToF -1.0 rate: {overall_rate:.1%}")

# per-sensor rate: if one sensor were dead it would be ~100%, not ~60%
for s in range(1, 6):
    cols = [f"tof_{s}_v{v}" for v in range(64)]
    rate = train_df.select(
        pl.mean_horizontal([(pl.col(c) == -1.0).cast(pl.Float32) for c in cols]).mean()
    ).item()
    print(f"  tof_{s}: {rate:.1%}")

# -1.0 rate by gesture: large variation = meaningful signal
gesture_tof = (
    train_df
    .with_columns(
        pl.mean_horizontal([(pl.col(c) == -1.0).cast(pl.Float32) for c in tof_cols])
          .alias("tof_missing_rate")
    )
    .group_by("gesture")
    .agg(pl.col("tof_missing_rate").mean().alias("avg_tof_missing_rate"))
    .sort("avg_tof_missing_rate", descending=True)
)
print(“\n-1.0 rate by gesture (highest = hand furthest from sensor):”)
print(gesture_tof)

# add per-sensor missing rate as features
train_df = train_df.with_columns([
    pl.mean_horizontal([(pl.col(f"tof_{s}_v{v}") == -1.0).cast(pl.Float32)
                        for v in range(64)]).alias(f"tof_{s}_missing_rate")
    for s in range(1, 6)
])
```

## Signal Character

11. What does a raw IMU signal (acc and rot) look like plotted over time for a BFRB vs. a non-BFRB gesture?

```{python}
#| echo: false
# pick one representative sequence per category
# update gesture names once you have the full list
bfrb_gesture     = "Above ear - pull hair"
non_bfrb_gesture = "Wave hello"

bfrb_seq = (
    train_df.filter(pl.col("gesture") == bfrb_gesture)
    .group_by("sequence_id").agg(pl.len()).sort("len", descending=True)
    .head(1)["sequence_id"][0]
)
non_bfrb_seq = (
    train_df.filter(pl.col("gesture") == non_bfrb_gesture)
    .group_by("sequence_id").agg(pl.len()).sort("len", descending=True)
    .head(1)["sequence_id"][0]
)

bfrb_data = train_df.filter(pl.col("sequence_id") == bfrb_seq).sort("sequence_counter")
non_bfrb_data = train_df.filter(pl.col("sequence_id") == non_bfrb_seq).sort("sequence_counter")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(7, 8), sharex=False)
fig.suptitle("Raw IMU Signal: BFRB vs. Non-BFRB", fontsize=14)

for col_idx, (data, label) in enumerate([(bfrb_data, f"BFRB\n{bfrb_gesture}"),
                                          (non_bfrb_data, f"Non-BFRB\n{non_bfrb_gesture}")]):
    t = data["sequence_counter"].to_numpy()

    # accelerometer
    ax = axes[0][col_idx]
    for col, color in zip(["acc_x", "acc_y", "acc_z"], ["r", "g", "b"]):
        ax.plot(t, data[col].to_numpy(), label=col, color=color, alpha=0.8)
    ax.set_title(f”Accelerometer: {label}”)
    ax.set_ylabel(“m/s²”)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)

    # rotation
    ax = axes[1][col_idx]
    for col, color in zip(["rot_w", "rot_x", "rot_y", "rot_z"], ["k", "r", "g", "b"]):
        ax.plot(t, data[col].to_numpy(), label=col, color=color, alpha=0.8)
    ax.set_title(f”Rotation (quaternion): {label}”)
    ax.set_ylabel("quaternion component")
    ax.set_xlabel("sequence counter (time step)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

bfrb_acc_range = (bfrb_data.select(pl.col(["acc_x","acc_y","acc_z"]).max() - pl.col(["acc_x","acc_y","acc_z"]).min())
                   .to_numpy().flatten().mean())
non_bfrb_acc_range = (non_bfrb_data.select(pl.col(["acc_x","acc_y","acc_z"]).max() - pl.col(["acc_x","acc_y","acc_z"]).min())
                       .to_numpy().flatten().mean())
print(f"BFRB ({bfrb_gesture}) avg acc range: {bfrb_acc_range:.2f} m/s²  |  "
      f"Non-BFRB ({non_bfrb_gesture}): {non_bfrb_acc_range:.2f} m/s²")
```

12. Do thermopile channels show distinct warmth signatures during touch-based BFRBs (e.g. hair pulling, skin picking) vs. non-contact gestures?

```{python}
#| echo: false
thm_cols = [f"thm_{i}" for i in range(1, 6)]

# mean thm by gesture
gesture_thm = (
    train_df
    .group_by("gesture")
    .agg(
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).mean().alias("avg_thm"),
        pl.col("is_bfrb").first()
    )
    .sort("avg_thm", descending=True)
)
print("Mean thermopile reading by gesture:")
print(gesture_thm)

bfrb_mean   = train_df.filter(pl.col("is_bfrb")).select(
    pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).mean()).item()
non_bfrb_mean = train_df.filter(~pl.col("is_bfrb")).select(
    pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).mean()).item()
print(f"\nBFRB mean thm: {bfrb_mean:.2f}°C  |  Non-BFRB mean thm: {non_bfrb_mean:.2f}°C  |  Gap: {bfrb_mean - non_bfrb_mean:.2f}°C")

# distribution + time-series plots
bfrb_thm = train_df.filter(pl.col("is_bfrb")).select(thm_cols).to_numpy().flatten()
non_bfrb_thm = train_df.filter(~pl.col("is_bfrb")).select(thm_cols).to_numpy().flatten()
bfrb_thm     = bfrb_thm[~np.isnan(bfrb_thm)]
non_bfrb_thm = non_bfrb_thm[~np.isnan(non_bfrb_thm)]

touch_seq = (
    train_df.filter(pl.col("gesture") == "Cheek - pinch skin")
    .group_by("sequence_id").agg(pl.len()).sort("len", descending=True)
    .head(1)["sequence_id"][0]
)
air_seq = (
    train_df.filter(pl.col("gesture") == "Write name in air")
    .group_by("sequence_id").agg(pl.len()).sort("len", descending=True)
    .head(1)["sequence_id"][0]
)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 5))
fig.suptitle("Thermopile Warmth: BFRB vs. Non-BFRB")

axes[0].hist(bfrb_thm, bins=60, alpha=0.6, label="BFRB", density=True)
axes[0].hist(non_bfrb_thm, bins=60, alpha=0.6, label="Non-BFRB", density=True)
axes[0].set_xlabel("Thermopile reading (°C)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Density")
axes[0].legend()
axes[0].set_title("Distribution of all thm readings")

colors = ["r", "g", "b", "orange", "purple"]
for seq_id, label in [(touch_seq, "touch"), (air_seq, "no contact")]:
    data = train_df.filter(pl.col("sequence_id") == seq_id).sort("sequence_counter")
    t = data["sequence_counter"].to_numpy()
    for col, c in zip(thm_cols, colors):
        axes[1].plot(t, data[col].to_numpy(), color=c,
                     label=f"{col} ({label})", alpha=0.7, linestyle="-" if label=="touch" else "--")

axes[1].set_title("Thermopile over time: touch vs. no-contact")
axes[1].set_xlabel("sequence counter")
axes[1].set_ylabel("°C")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

13. How spatially informative are the 8x8 ToF grids? Can you visualize a mean ToF frame per gesture class and see shape differences?

```{python}
#| echo: false
fig, axes = plt.subplots(5, 2, figsize=(5, 8))
fig.suptitle(“Mean ToF Frame (8x8) per Sensor: BFRB vs. Non-BFRB”)

for s_idx, sensor in enumerate(range(1, 6)):
    tof_cols_s = [f"tof_{sensor}_v{v}" for v in range(64)]

    for row_idx, (label, mask) in enumerate([("BFRB", pl.col("is_bfrb")),
                                              ("Non-BFRB", ~pl.col("is_bfrb"))]):
        # treat -1.0 as null so it doesn't drag the mean down
        mean_vals = (
            train_df.filter(mask)
            .select([
                pl.when(pl.col(c) == -1.0).then(None).otherwise(pl.col(c)).mean().alias(c)
                for c in tof_cols_s
            ])
            .row(0)
        )
        grid = np.array(mean_vals, dtype=float).reshape(8, 8)

        ax = axes[s_idx][row_idx]
        im = ax.imshow(grid, cmap="hot", aspect="auto")
        ax.set_title(f”tof_{sensor}: {label}”, fontsize=9)
        ax.set_xticks([])
        ax.set_yticks([])
        plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

14. Is there meaningful signal in the Pause or Transition phases, or is the Gesture phase doing most of the discriminative work?

```{python}
#| echo: false
print("Phases present:", train_df["phase"].unique().sort().to_list())

phase_signal = (
    train_df
    .with_columns(
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).alias("avg_thm"),
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c).abs() for c in ["acc_x","acc_y","acc_z"]]).alias("acc_mag"),
    )
    .group_by("phase", "is_bfrb")
    .agg(
        pl.col("avg_thm").mean(),
        pl.col("acc_mag").mean(),
        pl.len().alias("n_rows")
    )
    .sort("phase", "is_bfrb")
)
print(phase_signal)

# box plot: BFRB vs non-BFRB thm separation per phase
df_plot = (
    train_df
    .with_columns(pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).alias("avg_thm"))
    .select(["phase", "is_bfrb", "avg_thm"])
    .to_pandas()
)
phases = sorted(df_plot["phase"].unique())
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
positions, labels_x = [], []
for i, phase in enumerate(phases):
    for j, (flag, label, color) in enumerate([(False, "Non-BFRB", "orange"), (True, "BFRB", "steelblue")]):
        pos = i * 3 + j
        data = df_plot[(df_plot["phase"] == phase) & (df_plot["is_bfrb"] == flag)]["avg_thm"].dropna()
        bp = ax.boxplot(data, positions=[pos], widths=0.7, patch_artist=True,
                        boxprops=dict(facecolor=color, alpha=0.6),
                        medianprops=dict(color="black"),
                        whiskerprops=dict(alpha=0.4), capprops=dict(alpha=0.4),
                        flierprops=dict(alpha=0.05, markersize=1))
    labels_x.append(i * 3 + 0.5)

ax.set_xticks([i * 3 + 0.5 for i in range(len(phases))])
ax.set_xticklabels(phases)
ax.set_ylabel("avg thermopile (°C)")
ax.set_title("Thermopile Separation by Phase (orange=Non-BFRB, blue=BFRB)")
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
ax.legend(handles=[Patch(facecolor="steelblue", alpha=0.6, label="BFRB"),
                   Patch(facecolor="orange", alpha=0.6, label="Non-BFRB")])
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# acc_mag alone is flat; is there any IMU feature separating the classes?
# test jerk (rate of change of acceleration) and rotation variance, both per sequence
imu_seq_features = (
    train_df
    .with_columns(
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c).abs() for c in ["acc_x","acc_y","acc_z"]]).alias("acc_mag")
    )
    .sort("sequence_id", "sequence_counter")
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("acc_mag") - pl.col("acc_mag").shift(1).over("sequence_id")).abs().alias("acc_jerk")
    )
    .group_by("sequence_id")
    .agg(
        pl.col("acc_mag").std().alias("acc_mag_std"),
        pl.col("acc_jerk").mean().alias("acc_jerk_mean"),
        pl.col("rot_x").std().alias("rot_x_std"),
        pl.col("rot_y").std().alias("rot_y_std"),
        pl.col("rot_z").std().alias("rot_z_std"),
        pl.col("is_bfrb").first(),
    )
)

candidate_features = ["acc_mag_std", "acc_jerk_mean", "rot_x_std", "rot_y_std", "rot_z_std"]
feature_comparison = (
    imu_seq_features
    .group_by("is_bfrb")
    .agg([pl.col(f).mean().alias(f) for f in candidate_features])
)
print("Sequence-level IMU feature means, BFRB vs Non-BFRB:")
print(feature_comparison)

# effect size (Cohen's d) per feature to rank discriminative power
pdf_imu = imu_seq_features.to_pandas()
print("\nEffect size (Cohen's d) per candidate IMU feature:")
for f in candidate_features:
    g1 = pdf_imu[pdf_imu["is_bfrb"]][f].dropna()
    g0 = pdf_imu[~pdf_imu["is_bfrb"]][f].dropna()
    pooled_std = np.sqrt(((g1.std()**2) + (g0.std()**2)) / 2)
    d = (g1.mean() - g0.mean()) / pooled_std if pooled_std > 0 else 0
    print(f"  {f}: d = {d:.3f}")
```

## Subject and Demographic Variation

15. Do signal ranges vary substantially across subjects, what does subject-level normalization look like?

```{python}
#| echo: false
subj_stats = (
    train_df
    .group_by("subject")
    .agg([
        pl.col("acc_x").mean().alias("acc_x_mean"),
        pl.col("acc_x").std().alias("acc_x_std"),
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).mean().alias("thm_mean"),
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).std().alias("thm_std"),
        pl.col("rot_w").is_null().mean().alias("rot_null_rate"),
        pl.col("thm_5").is_null().mean().alias("thm5_null_rate"),
        pl.len().alias("n_rows"),
        pl.col("sequence_id").n_unique().alias("n_sequences"),
    ])
)

thm_mean_vals = subj_stats["thm_mean"].drop_nulls()
print(f"Per-subject thm_mean: min={thm_mean_vals.min():.1f}°C  max={thm_mean_vals.max():.1f}°C  "
      f"range={thm_mean_vals.max() - thm_mean_vals.min():.1f}°C  std={thm_mean_vals.std():.2f}°C")

# apply subject-level z-score normalization
train_df = train_df.with_columns([
    ((pl.col(c) - pl.col(c).mean().over("subject")) /
     pl.col(c).std().over("subject")).alias(f"{c}_znorm")
    for c in thm_cols
])

# show before/after
sample_subj = subj_stats.sort("thm_mean").head(1)["subject"][0]
raw_mean = train_df.filter(pl.col("subject") == sample_subj)["thm_1"].mean()
znorm_mean = train_df.filter(pl.col("subject") == sample_subj)["thm_1_znorm"].mean()
print(f"\nExample (coldest subject {sample_subj}): raw thm_1 mean = {raw_mean:.2f}  znorm mean = {znorm_mean:.2f}")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 4))
fig.suptitle("Subject-Level Signal Variation")
axes[0].hist(subj_stats["thm_mean"].to_numpy(), bins=40)
axes[0].set_xlabel("Per-subject mean thermopile (°C)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("# subjects")
axes[0].set_title(f"Thermopile mean (range {thm_mean_vals.max()-thm_mean_vals.min():.1f}°C)")
axes[1].hist(subj_stats["thm_std"].to_numpy(), bins=40)
axes[1].set_xlabel("Per-subject std thermopile (°C)")
axes[1].set_title("Thermopile std across subjects")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

joining demographics columns into train and test df's

```{python}
#| echo: false
demo_df = pl.read_csv("../data/train_demographics.csv")
train_df = train_df.join(demo_df, on="subject", how="left")

test_demo_df = pl.read_csv("../data/test_demographics.csv")
test_df = test_df.join(test_demo_df, on="subject", how="left")

# resolve the handedness confound found in Q16: left-handed subjects show a different
# acc_x orientation, which would otherwise be encoded as noise by any rolling-window feature.
# mirror the x-axis (acc_x, rot_x) for left-handed subjects so all subjects share one orientation convention.
before_gap = (
    train_df.group_by("handedness")
    .agg(pl.col("acc_x").mean().alias("acc_x_mean"))
    .sort("handedness")
)
print("acc_x_mean by handedness BEFORE mirroring:")
print(before_gap)

for df_name, df in [("train_df", train_df), ("test_df", test_df)]:
    mirrored = df.with_columns([
        pl.when(pl.col("handedness") == 0).then(-pl.col("acc_x")).otherwise(pl.col("acc_x")).alias("acc_x"),
        pl.when(pl.col("handedness") == 0).then(-pl.col("rot_x")).otherwise(pl.col("rot_x")).alias("rot_x"),
    ])
    if df_name == "train_df":
        train_df = mirrored
    else:
        test_df = mirrored

after_gap = (
    train_df.group_by("handedness")
    .agg(pl.col("acc_x").mean().alias("acc_x_mean"))
    .sort("handedness")
)
print("\nacc_x_mean by handedness AFTER mirroring:")
print(after_gap)
```

17. Are any subjects outliers whose data looks corrupted or implausible?

```{python}
#| echo: false
pdf = subj_demo.to_pandas()

for col in ["thm_mean", "acc_x_mean"]:
    pdf[f"{col}_z"] = (pdf[col] - pdf[col].mean()) / pdf[col].std()

outliers = pdf[
    (pdf["thm_mean_z"].abs() > 3) |
    (pdf["acc_x_mean_z"].abs() > 3) |
    (pdf["rot_null_rate"] > 0.5) |
    (pdf["thm5_null_rate"] == 1.0)
][["subject", "thm_mean", "thm_mean_z", "acc_x_mean", "acc_x_mean_z",
   "n_rows", "rot_null_rate", "thm5_null_rate", "age", "handedness"]].sort_values("thm_mean")

print(f"Flagged outlier subjects: {len(outliers)}")
print(outliers.to_string(index=False))

# flag suspect subjects (those with thm_mean z < -3)
suspect_subjects = set(outliers[outliers["thm_mean_z"] < -3]["subject"].tolist())
print(f"Suspect subjects (thermopile z < -3): {suspect_subjects}")

train_df = train_df.with_columns(
    pl.col("subject").is_in(suspect_subjects).cast(pl.Int8).alias("is_suspect_subject")
)
```

## Validation

Does the Q12 thermopile warmth gap (BFRB vs. Non-BFRB) survive excluding the suspect subjects flagged in Q17? SUBJ_028998 and SUBJ_036405 read 4–5°C colder than everyone else and are disproportionately likely to fall in the non-BFRB baseline by chance, which could be inflating the apparent gap.

```{python}
#| echo: false
def thm_gap(df, label):
    bfrb_mean = df.filter(pl.col("is_bfrb")).select(
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).mean()).item()
    non_bfrb_mean = df.filter(~pl.col("is_bfrb")).select(
        pl.mean_horizontal([pl.col(c) for c in thm_cols]).mean()).item()
    gap = bfrb_mean - non_bfrb_mean
    print(f"{label}: BFRB={bfrb_mean:.2f}°C  Non-BFRB={non_bfrb_mean:.2f}°C  Gap={gap:.2f}°C")
    return gap

gap_all = thm_gap(train_df, "All subjects (original Q12 result)")
gap_clean = thm_gap(train_df.filter(~pl.col("subject").is_in(suspect_subjects)), "Excluding suspect subjects")

pct_change = abs(gap_all - gap_clean) / gap_all * 100
print(f"\nGap change after exclusion: {pct_change:.1f}%")
```
